name: end-trigger-8
description: THE END TRIGGER AT 8, AGAINST THE SHIPPED 6 (v31, 02/09/2026). The single paired arm for risk 1 of the whole v31 pass: ACTION INFLATION. The bonus slot now buys a WHOLE CORE ACTION for one card - the Wheat door is a free Harvest, the Dairy door a free Build - and meeples add uncapped free actions on top of that, one at a time at the start of a turn. Turns are materially more powerful than v30's, so the same 6 deliveries arrive in fewer turns and the game gets shorter while scores go up. 8 is the first correction to try, and the trigger is the right lever because it is the only number that lengthens the game without touching what anything is worth. READ IT IN THIS ORDER, AND READ EVERY LINE PER SEAT COUNT, because the trigger is FLAT across seat counts and 6 is half the 2-seat island's 12 delivery spaces but only a quarter of the 4-seat island's 24: (1) turns per game and actions resolved per turn - the second is the number the whole pass moves and the reason this arm exists; (2) the winning score, which should fall back toward the pre-v31 band if the shipped 6 was simply too short; (3) island fill fraction at the end, which at 8 should climb and must not reach 100% at 2 seats, where the board is smallest relative to the trigger; (4) unfinished games and supply locks, which are the failure mode of a longer game - a deck that runs out is a different problem from a game that ends too soon; (5) the meeple economy, earned against spent, because a longer game gives a seat more turns in which to burn a meeple and a pile that clears at 8 but not at 6 says the start-of-turn restriction is the real constraint rather than the pool. DO NOT DIAL THIS BEFORE ACTIONS-PER-TURN HAS BEEN MEASURED. Setting the clock against an unknown is how the flat island's first three fixes went wrong. IF 2p IS THE ONLY SEAT COUNT THAT MISBEHAVES, the answer is not a bigger flat number: it is a per-seat row here or a smaller 2p island in slotsBySeats. overlays/end-trigger.sweep.json is the full ladder from 4 to 8 when one paired reading is not enough. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved.
